findings.title: Retrieved from Cache
findings.evidence: The content was retrieved from a shared cache. If the response data is sensitive, personal or user-specific, this may result in sensitive information being leaked. In some cases, this may even result in a user gaining complete control of the session of another user, depending on the configuration of the caching components in use in their environment. This is primarily an issue where caching servers such as "proxy" caches are configured on the local network. This configuration is typically found in corporate or educational environments, for instance.

extra.solution:
Validate that the response does not contain sensitive, personal or user-specific information. If it does, consider the use of the following HTTP response headers, to limit, or prevent the content being stored and retrieved from the cache by another user:
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private
Pragma: no-cache
Expires: 0
This configuration directs both HTTP 1.0 and HTTP 1.1 compliant caching servers to not store the response, and to not retrieve the response (without validation) from the cache, in response to a similar request.

correlate.executive_summary: The assessment discovered several security and configuration issues on juiceshop.cortexlab.org.in. Most findings are informational or low/medium risk misconfigurations (missing security headers, exposed /ftp path, caching concerns, CORS) but multiple high-severity issues were reported by nmap's HTTP NSE scripts (including LFI hints for phpMyAdmin and multiple denial-of-service related issues). Cloudflare is present as a proxy in front of the site which may affect direct fingerprinting and exploitability. Conflicting header observations were noted (e.g. X-Frame-Options), so some findings remain suspected and require manual verification. Prioritized remediation should address confirmed high-risk items and then the medium/low configuration weaknesses.

findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) header not set
findings.evidence: va (zap): "Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set" reported (occurrences: 76) stating CSP not present; recon: "Missing security header: content-security-policy" (confirmed). Both agents observed responses without a CSP header.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header not set
findings.evidence: va (zap): "Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set" (occurrences: 94) and recon: "Missing security header: strict-transport-security" (confirmed) indicating responses do not set HSTS.

findings.title: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) / cross-domain misconfiguration
findings.evidence: va (zap): "Cross-Domain Misconfiguration" (occurrences: 94) reported potential CORS misconfiguration; nmap (http-cors NSE) listed allowed methods (HEAD GET POST PUT DELETE PATCH) in its results. No explicit vulnerable origin value was recorded; manual verification required.

findings.title: Exposed /ftp directory (listed in robots.txt)
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 200 on /ftp (differs from baseline 404) — body observed; nmap (http-robots.txt) reported robots.txt disallow entry for /ftp; va (zap) also enumerated /ftp endpoints in scanning output. robots.txt entry suggests operator intentionally hid this path and reconnaissance confirmed it is accessible.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options / clickjacking protection inconsistent or missing
findings.evidence: va (nikto): reported "The anti-clickjacking X-Frame-Options header is not present." (nikto GET to http://juiceshop.cortexlab.org.in:443). nmap (http-security-headers NSE) output shows "X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN" for some responses. Observations conflict between scanners; manual verification required to determine scope and consistency across endpoints.

findings.title: Cloudflare proxy detected (server fingerprint)
findings.evidence: nmap service/version detection: "http (Cloudflare http proxy)" on ports 80/443/8080/8443 (confirmed); recon: "Technology fingerprint" detected cloudflare. Also nikto reported cf-ray header. Indicates Cloudflare is fronting the site.

findings.title: Cache-control directives missing or inconsistent (retrieved from shared cache)
findings.evidence: va (zap): "Re-examine Cache-control Directives" (occurrences: 20) and "Retrieved from Cache" for /robots.txt — scanner noted content retrieved from a shared cache which may leak sensitive data if caching is misconfigured.

findings.title: phpMyAdmin grab_globals.lib.php - Local File Inclusion (LFI) reported by NSE
findings.evidence: nmap (http-phpmyadmin-dir-traversal NSE): reported "VULNERABLE: phpMyAdmin grab_globals.lib.php subform Parameter Traversal Local File Inclusion" and referenced CVE-2005-3299 in the script output. NSE script state shown as UNKNOWN (unable to fully test) but presented the LFI description.

findings.title: Apache byterange filter DoS (CVE-2011-3192) reported by NSE
findings.evidence: nmap (http-vuln-cve2011-3192 NSE): reported "VULNERABLE: Apache byterange filter DoS" and referenced CVE-2011-3192 with state VULNERABLE in script output (includes references and disclosure date).

findings.title: Slowloris-style DoS susceptibility reported
findings.evidence: nmap (http-slowloris-check NSE): reported "VULNERABLE: Slowloris DOS attack" with state "LIKELY VULNERABLE" and referenced CVE-2007-6750 in the script output.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header not set
findings.evidence: recon: "Missing security header: referrer-policy" (confirmed) — responses did not set a Referrer-Policy header to control referer leakage.

correlate.deduplication_notes: Merged duplicate observations about missing Content-Security-Policy (va zap + recon) into one finding. Merged duplicate Strict-Transport-Security/HSTS observations (va zap + recon). Combined robots.txt /ftp related findings from recon, nmap (http-robots.txt) and va into a single exposed-path finding for /ftp. Collated multiple security-header observations (nikto, nmap, va) and noted inconsistencies (X-Frame-Options conflict) rather than elevating confidence. Grouped cache-control and retrieved-from-cache alerts from va together. Left distinct nmap NSE script results (phpMyAdmin LFI, Apache byterange DoS, Slowloris) as separate findings because each reports a different issue and includes its own CVE reference in the NSE output.
